definition: a character whose evil actions or motives are important to a story
hook: A villain used to just mean the guy who worked the fields.
modernAnchor: Every story needs one, the mustache-twirling, plan-hatching villain we love to hate.
journey: In Latin, villanus simply named a farmhand, someone who worked the fields around a country villa.
Nobles saw peasants as coarse and dishonest, so villain drifted from farmhand toward scoundrel and criminal.
By Shakespeare's day, villain meant a schemer, no longer someone who simply worked the land.
Class prejudice wrote the definition. The word never forgot its start, plowing fields, not planning crimes.
